body.statement:
For the fixed class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), there are a law \(P^\circ\in\mathcal M_1(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\) and a constant \(\delta\in(0,1)\) such that, for every \(0<C_m<\infty\), the unique admissible fit \(\widehat m\), and \(x=1\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}P^{\circ\otimes n}\{\mathcal G_n(1;C_m,\widehat m)^c\}\ge e^{-\delta}>2e^{-1}.
\]
Thus no finite \(C_m\) makes the \(2e^{-1}\) complement-probability bound for \(\mathcal G_n(1;C_m,\widehat m)\) uniform over \(\mathcal M_1(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\) for this fixed local-polynomial nuisance protocol.
body.proof_tex:
Set \(d=1\) and \(\theta=+1\).  By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:attainable\text{-}margin\text{-}rectangle}\), choose \(a\) in the interior of the certified chart interval and fix \(t\in(0,t_0]\) so that the nonlinear chart law
\[
P^\circ=P_{a,t,+}
\]
belongs to \(\mathcal M_1(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\).  Under Definition \(\mathrm{def:hermite\text{-}chart}\), the true-direction query \(b=+1\) has
\[
C=Z,\qquad E=aZ+t(Z^2-1)+s_{a,t}\xi,qquad Z,\xi\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp},qquad Z,\xi\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Because \(\mathbb E(\xi\mid Z)=0\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:population\text{-}regressions}\), which is an input to the admissible protocol, gives
\[
m(z)=\mathbb E_{P^\circ}(E\mid Z=z)=az+t(z^2-1).
\]

Fix one of the four regression folds in Definition \(\mathrm{def:balanced\text{-}four\text{-}fold\text{-}allocation}\), and denote its cardinality by \(m_n\).  Balance gives \(m_n/n\to1/4\).  Put \(h=h_n\).  From Definition \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}class}\),
\[
h=\{\max(1,\lfloor n/4\rfloor)\}^{-1/(2\beta+1)},
\qquad
m_nh\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
where the second conclusion uses \(\beta>1/2\), hence in particular \(\beta>0\).

Choose a constant \(\delta\) with
\[
0<\delta<1-\log 2.
\]
Then \(e^{-\delta}>2e^{-1}\).  Let \(\varphi_0(z)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-z^2/2}\) be the standard-normal density and, for \(z\ge2h\), define
\[
F_n(z)=P^\circ\{Z\in[z-2h,z+2h]\}.
\]
The map \(F_n\) is continuous, tends to zero as \(z\to\infty\), and is strictly decreasing on \((2h,\infty)\), since
\[
F_n'(z)=\varphi_0(z+2h)-\varphi_0(z-2h)<0.
\]
Moreover, \(m_nF_n(2h)\asymp m_nh\to\infty\).  The intermediate value theorem therefore gives, for every sufficiently large \(n\), a unique \(z_n>2h\) such that, with
\[
J_n=[z_n-2h,z_n+2h],
\qquad
m_nP^\circ(Z\in J_n)=\delta.
\]

The integral mean-value theorem supplies \(\zeta_n\in J_n\) for which
\[
4h\varphi_0(\zeta_n)=P^\circ(Z\in J_n)=\frac{\delta}{m_n}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\zeta_n^2
=2\log\!\left(\frac{4m_nh}{\delta\sqrt{2\pi}}\right)
=\frac{4\beta}{2\beta+1}\log n+O(1).
\]
In particular, \(\zeta_n\to\infty\), \(z_n=O(\sqrt{\log n})\), and \(z_nh\to0\).  Since \(|z_n-\zeta_n|\le2h\),
\[
|z_n^2-\zeta_n^2|
\le 2h(z_n+\zeta_n)=o(1),
\]
and hence
\[
z_n^2=\frac{4\beta}{2\beta+1}\log n+O(1).
\]
The coefficient \(4\beta/(2\beta+1)\) is strictly smaller than \(2\), while Definition \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}class}\) fixes
\[
T_n^2=\frac{8\log(n\vee3)}{c_0}
\]
with \(0<c_0<1\).  It follows that \(z_n+3h/2<T_n\) for every sufficiently large \(n\).

Define the smaller interval
\[
A_n=[z_n-h/2,z_n+h/2].
\]
For any \(x,y\in J_n\),
\[
\frac{\varphi_0(x)}{\varphi_0(y)}
=\exp\{(y^2-x^2)/2\},
\qquad
|x^2-y^2|\le8z_nh+16h^2.
\]
Because \(z_nh+h^2\to0\), the ratio of the maximum and minimum of \(\varphi_0\) on \(J_n\) tends to one.  Since the lengths of \(A_n\) and \(J_n\) are respectively \(h\) and \(4h\),
\[
\frac{P^\circ(Z\in A_n)}{P^\circ(Z\in J_n)}\longrightarrow\frac14.
\]
Using \(P^\circ(Z\in J_n)=\delta/m_n\) and \(m_n\le n\), there is a constant \(c_A>0\) such that
\[
P^\circ(Z\in A_n)\ge\frac{c_A}{n}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Let \(E_n\) be the event that the selected regression fold contains no predictor value in \(J_n\).  The observations are independent by the sampling model, so
\[
P^{\circ\otimes n}(E_n)
=\left(1-\frac{\delta}{m_n}\right)^{m_n}.
\]
Indeed, the probability for each of the \(m_n\) fold observations to avoid \(J_n\) is \(1-\delta/m_n\).  Since
\[
m_n\log\left(1-\frac{\delta}{m_n}\right)\longrightarrow-\delta,
\]
we have
\[
P^{\circ\otimes n}(E_n)\longrightarrow e^{-\delta}.
\]

We next evaluate the unique fit specified by Definition \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}class}\).  If \(z\in A_n\), then \(|z|\le T_n-h\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), so the interior kernel \(K_{z,n}=K_{\mathrm{LP}}\) is used.  Its support property implies that a nonzero observation weight requires
\[
|Z_i-z|\le h,
\]
which in turn implies
\[
Z_i\in[z_n-3h/2,z_n+3h/2]\subset J_n.
\]
Thus, on \(E_n\), every data-fit term in the local-polynomial objective is zero for every \(z\in A_n\).  The remaining objective is the strictly positive ridge
\[
n^{-2}\sum_{q=0}^{p_{\mathrm{LP}}}a_q^2,
\]
whose unique minimizer is \(a_q=0\) for every \(q\).  Clipping fixes zero, and therefore the selected foldwise true-direction fit satisfies
\[
\widehat m(z)=0\qquad\text{for every }z\in A_n
\]
on \(E_n\).

Because \(t>0\), \(a>0\), and \(z_n\to\infty\), the displayed formula for \(m\) yields constants \(c_m,c_z>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\inf_{z\in A_n}|m(z)|
\ge c_m z_n^2
\ge c_z\log n.
\]
Combining this inequality with the lower probability bound for \(A_n\), on \(E_n\) we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\widehat m-m\|_{L^4(P^\circ_C)}
&\ge
\left\{\int_{A_n}|m(z)|^4\,dP^\circ_C(z)\right\}^{1/4}\\
&\ge c_E n^{-1/4}\log n
\end{aligned}
\]
for a fixed constant \(c_E>0\).

By Definition \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}good\text{-}event}\), when \(d=1\) and \(x=1\), its right-hand threshold is
\[
C_m\left(r_n+\sqrt{\frac{1+\log2}{n}}\right).
\]
Definition \(r_n=n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) and the strict inequality \(\beta>1/2\) give
\[
\frac{\beta}{2\beta+1}>\frac14,
\qquad
r_n+\sqrt{\frac{1+\log2}{n}}
=o\!\left(n^{-1/4}\log n\right).
\]
Hence, for every fixed \(0<C_m<\infty\), the event \(E_n\) is contained in \(\mathcal G_n(1;C_m,\widehat m)^c\) for all sufficiently large \(n\): the maximum defining \(\mathcal G_n\) includes the selected rotation and true-direction query just bounded.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
P^{\circ\otimes n}\{\mathcal G_n(1;C_m,\widehat m)^c\}
&\ge \lim_{n\to\infty}P^{\circ\otimes n}(E_n)\\
&=e^{-\delta}>2e^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since the same fixed member \(P^\circ\) works for every finite \(C_m>0\), no such constant yields the claimed \(2e^{-1}\) complement-probability bound uniformly over \(\mathcal M_1(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\) for the specified local-polynomial regression-good event.  The proof makes no assertion about statistics outside that fixed nuisance protocol.
